correctness.rationale: For m>=3 and theta>0, all-r-coordinate lower-tail events have exact mass t(r-(r-1)t^theta)^(-1/theta). Every wrong-orientation event with at least two constrained coordinates contains either a lower/upper pair with mass O(t^(2+theta)) or an upper/upper pair with mass O(t^2). Numerator and conditional denominator therefore have the exact strictly positive coefficients stated in RESULT. The resulting edge odds are ratios of positive weights; square-cycle identities are necessary, and graph path-independence makes them sufficient and yields unique normalized weights and theta. The separate Python standard-library checker tests rational examples and exact finite-event probabilities, without treating finite checks as proof.

originality.rationale: The initial March 2024 paper presents bivariate rotated mixtures; its February 2025 multivariate revision defines the same conditional extreme-tail observable, but its component-weighted linear calculation is not generally valid because the denominator depends on the orientation weights. The new first-order conditional calculation, hypercube edge-sum and square-cycle conditions, and unique inverse recover the exact model-specific image. The concrete uniform three-dimensional example yields actual value 1/3 rather than the linear-expression value 1/12. Published general pairwise matrix realization results involve different observables; no covering inverse theorem was located. Priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: The result uses a common Clayton parameter, whereas the originating paper permits parameters to vary by orientation.
A generic theorem on mixtures or exact graph odds might be adaptable in hindsight; no exact published implication for these conditioned-tail observables was identified.

value.rationale: The exact intrinsic image and inverse theorem gives model identifiability from a natural set of conditional extreme-risk observables alone, not from the full copula density. Common edge sums recover the tail parameter, and face tests reject locally plausible but globally incompatible conditional tails; the explicit m=3 witness demonstrates a meaningful falsifiable restriction. This is a complete parametric classification for a motivated high-dimensional extremal model and not a routine numerical recomputation.
